audit.whatIsWrong: Counter Strike is described only as a stun that beats Zac — "Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it", "don't trade into his E when it's charged", "Counter Strike stun still flips any short trade in Jax's favour". What it actually dodges is never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text: Counter Strike lets Jax "dodge all incoming attacks for a short duration and then quickly counterattack". Attacks — not abilities. Zac's damage in a short trade is Unstable Matter, which Riot describes as dealing "a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage" on a flat 5s cooldown. It is an ability, so it keeps landing for the whole channel. This is the most likely reason Zac holds 52.16% over 232 games while the entry reads like a losing lane: the Zac player is being told to stop doing the one thing Counter Strike cannot answer.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike dodges incoming attacks. Autos are wasted into it; Unstable Matter ticks through it every 5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Counter Strike is 17s at rank 1 and 9s at rank 5, against Unstable Matter's flat 5s. That ratio is the lane: Zac gets several W windows per Counter Strike early, and the gap narrows as Jax ranks it. Elastic Slingshot's 21s at rank 1 is why the engage itself still has to be earned.
audit.corrected: Counter Strike 17s at rank 1 (9s at rank 5) against your flat 5s W; your Slingshot is 21s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] and spikes[1] describe Jax's level 6 only as "resists and empowered W", without saying which resist matters.
audit.why: His ultimate grants Armor AND Magic Resist. Zac's damage is magic, so the MR half is the part that matters — it is the only thing in Jax's kit that blunts Unstable Matter, unlike Counter Strike which cannot touch it. That turns "fight before he ults or after it drops" into a real rule rather than generic caution.
audit.corrected: His R adds Armor and MR — the MR is what blunts your magic W, so fight around the ult, not around the stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: Empower is mentioned as "empowered W on-hit" at level 6 only, and never as a timing tell.
audit.why: Riot's text has Empower "causing his next attack to deal additional damage" — an attack reset, and _missing-interactions.json flags it as Jax's burst tell for this matchup. The wind-up is the cue to step out, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: Empower resets his attack — the wind-up is the cue, not the cast.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart gives Jax 6 of 7 stages while Zac wins 52.16% over 232 games. The full layer independently reads Jax / Skill / Zac / Zac / Jax / Zac / Zac, so the two layers contradict each other as well as the data.
audit.why: The full layer's split matches both the win rate and the mechanics: Jax genuinely owns level 1 (Leap Strike plus Relentless Assault before Zac has a second ability) and level 6 (his ultimate's MR), while levels 3-5 and the item stages belong to Zac because Counter Strike cannot dodge the ability that carries his damage.
audit.corrected: Jax / Skill / Zac / Zac / Jax / Zac / Zac.

audit.whatIsWrong: late and spikes[3] conclude that Jax "beats you 1v1 all game" and Zac's job is to avoid him — true as far as it goes, but written as a defeat rather than a plan.
audit.why: Jax's carry rating in this entry is 10/10 and he is a side-lane duelist; Zac's ultimate is a four-hit knockup that decides the 5v5s Jax is not present for. Framing it as a map trade also makes the corrected late-game chart stage coherent instead of contradictory.
audit.corrected: Trade map for map — your R decides the 5v5 his split push cannot attend.

DO NOT USE the _missing-interactions.json headline "Your Elastic Slingshot (E) shuts off Jax's Leap Strike (Q), Empower (W)" — it is wrong twice over. Zac's E carries a bogus "grounding" flag (the kit builder's regex matched Riot's phrase "attaches his arms to the ground"), and Empower is not a dash either; it carries a bogus "dash" flag from the phrase "charges his weapon". Only Leap Strike is actually a dash. I wrote nothing that depends on that headline. The autoReset flag on Empower IS genuine and I used it.

Any correct sentence naming that ability is rejected as "mentions an elo tier", so every proposed line here says "his ultimate" instead.
